key_concept: In base-catalysed aldol condensation, the $\beta$-hydroxy carbonyl dehydrates by the E1cB route, where the $\alpha$-H is lost, so the new C=C always forms between the $\alpha$- and $\beta$-carbons ($\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated product) and only carbons bearing $\alpha$-H can form enolates.
steps: In 2,2-dimethylcyclopentanone the $\alpha$-carbon C-2 is quaternary (gem-dimethyl, no H). The only enolisable position is C-5 ($CH_2$). PhCHO has no $\alpha$-H, so it can act only as the electrophile.
Cross aldol: the C-5 enolate adds to PhCHO, and dehydration by E1cB gives the benzylidene ketone $C_5=CH-Ph$. Both geometric isomers, E and Z, can form, so options (2) and (4) are obtainable.
Self aldol: the C-5 enolate of one ketone attacks C=O (C-1) of a second ketone molecule. This gives a $\beta$-hydroxy ketone in which the $C-OH$ carbon is C-1 of the second ring.

On heating with base, the E1cB elimination removes the acidic $\alpha$-H at C-5 of the first ring together with the $\beta$-OH. The C=C therefore forms between C-5 (ring 1) and C-1 (ring 2), giving the conjugated exocyclic cyclopentylidene ketone of option (3).

Option (1) has its C=C inside the second ring, i.e. at the $\beta,\gamma$-position, not conjugated with C=O, while the $\alpha$-carbon remains $sp^3$. This is not the $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated product an aldol condensation gives, so (1) cannot be obtained.
final_answer: Option (1): 2,2-Dimethylcyclopentanone whose C-5 is singly bonded to C-1 of a 5,5-dimethylcyclopent-1-ene ring (non-conjugated, $\beta,\gamma$-unsaturated product)
why_not_others: Options (2) and (4) are the E and Z cross-aldol (Claisen–Schmidt) products with PhCHO. Option (3) is the conjugated self-aldol condensation product of the ketone, so all three are genuine aldol condensation products.
common_trap: Students often think self-condensation is impossible in the presence of PhCHO, or treat (2) and (4) as the same compound and mark one of them, ignoring that the double bond must end up $\alpha,\beta$ to C=O.
time_saving_tip: Check every option for a C=C directly conjugated with C=O at the $\alpha$-carbon. The one lacking $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturation is the answer.
